locator: Why is there a reserve on my account?
quote: A reserve may be implemented if Stripe thinks that your business represents a higher than acceptable level of risk.

locator: What types of reserves are there?
quote: Stripe uses two types of reserve: fixed and rolling. Either one can also include a balance transfer. The email Stripe sends you will tell you which one applies to your account.
With a fixed reserve, a specific percentage of funds from each new sale is held until a future release date. On that date, all the funds are returned to your available balance.

With a rolling reserve, a percentage of funds from each new sale is held back for a set length of time, measured from the date of that sale. Each reserved amount is released on its own schedule, such that money flows in and out of the reserve continuously.

Because both a fixed and a rolling reserve only affect new sales, they take time to build up the reserved amount. To cover that gap, Stripe may also move a percentage of your balance into reserve when the reserve is initially applied.

locator: Will I lose money? Is this a fine?
quote: No. A reserve is not a fee or a fine, and you do not lose the money. Stripe simply sets a portion of your funds aside for a time instead of paying it out right away.
